title: IFR Equipment: GRABCARD + the Checks
hook: Is this airplane even legal for IFR? Grab a card.

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds. I F R equipment: your day V F R stuff, night stuff after dark, plus GRAB CARD.
Generator. Radios. Altimeter — the sensitive kind. Ball. Clock with seconds. Attitude. Rate of turn. Directional gyro.
The paperwork twins: ninety-one four-eleven, altimeter and static. Ninety-one four-thirteen, transponder. Every twenty-four calendar months. They expire quietly — check the logbooks, not the vibes.
GRAB CARD for the panel, twenty-four months for the plumbing. Can't prove it, can't file it.
Ninety-one two-oh-five, paragraph d. Bring a flashlight.

quiz.question: In GRABCARD, the second A stands for:
quiz.explanation: G-R-A-B-C-A-R-D: Generator, Radios, Altimeter, Ball, Clock, Attitude indicator, Rate of turn, Directional gyro. (91.205(d))

quiz.question: The altimeter/static system (91.411) and transponder (91.413) checks are required every:
quiz.explanation: Both inspections run on a 24-calendar-month clock — and IFR flight requires the 91.411 check to be current.

quiz.question: The clock required for IFR must display:
choices: Hours, minutes, seconds — sweep hand or digital
quiz.explanation: 91.205(d) requires a clock showing hours, minutes, and seconds with a sweep-second pointer or digital presentation.
